request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now have a contact. `bin/e2e` passed all 4 tests in the spec. After that I re-wrapped one comment in a YAML file and didn't run the tests again.

**How it behaves**
- **Storing:** spaces around the contact are removed and it is lower-cased, so `" Ada@X "` is saved as `ada@x`. A blank contact counts as none.
- **Duplicates:** a contact another person on the sheet already has is refused on both add and edit. The server returns a 409, the form shows its error, and nothing is saved or audited. A database unique index on sheet and contact also blocks two people saving the same contact at the same moment.
- **Audit:** `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<contact>` when one was given. `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<contact>` only when the contact changed, and with an empty `contact=` when it was cleared.
- **Other ways of changing a person:** quick-add creates people with no contact. Bulk grade, retire and hold leave the contact as it is.

**What changed**
- **Database:** new migration `V52__person_contact.sql` adds a `contact` column and the unique index.
- **Server:** the `Person`, `PersonRequest` and `PersonValues` records carry the contact, and `PersonRepository` saves and reads it. Two new check steps refuse a taken contact, `CheckPersonContact` for adding and `CheckPersonRecontact` for editing, and are wired into the add and edit endpoints `people.POST.yml` and `{personId}.PUT.yml`. A new `DuplicatePersonContactException` has a handler that returns the 409. `ApplyPerson` also records the contact the person had before an edit.
- **Front end:** the person form has a `person-form-contact` field and each row shows `person-contact`.

The form shows the same error for a taken name and a taken contact: "That name or contact is already in use on this sheet." The error response doesn't say which one clashed.
